title: Poll an asynchronous vCenter VM clone from a VCF PowerCLI module
prompt:
Complete src/VcfVCenterAutomation/VcfVCenterAutomation.psm1. The PowerShell module must use the preinstalled VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager PowerCLI module declared by its manifest; do not install, copy, or vendor VMware modules. Preserve the public commands and parameter types documented in README.md. Implement only the two vSphere Automation API operations in docs/contract.json, which was extracted from the pinned official VCF 9.1 vCenter OpenAPI specification recorded in docs/official_sources.json.

Invoke-VcfVmClone must submit Vcenter.VM_clone$Task and treat the 202 response as a task identifier, then poll that exact identifier with Cis.Tasks_get until SUCCEEDED or FAILED. PENDING, RUNNING, and BLOCKED are non-terminal. Return the successful task result and polling evidence, throw on FAILED or an unexpected state, and enforce the supplied timeout and polling interval. Do not treat HTTP 202 as completion.

Construct the clone JSON from the bound parameters. source and name are required. Create placement only when at least one placement parameter was bound, and include only its bound members. Omit every other unset optional field instead of sending null, an empty string, an empty object, or an empty array. Poll Cis.Tasks_get without its optional spec query parameter. Send the exact methods, /api paths, fixed query values, JSON media type, and vmware-api-session-id authentication required by the focused contract. The acceptance verifier compares the raw wire form: the clone body must be compact JSON (no extra whitespace) with source before name, sent with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a Content-Length matching the UTF-8 body, and every request must send Accept: application/json while GET task reads carry no body and no Content-Type. Support both an authenticated VMware.Sdk.OpenApi.Cmdlets.IServerConnection and the documented loopback-friendly session-token connection form. Fail non-2xx responses. Do not contact a live VMware endpoint and do not modify protected files. Run python3 tests/verify.py.
scenario: a clone submission returns HTTP 202 with a task identifier, so the module polls Cis.Tasks_get through PENDING and RUNNING and returns the SUCCEEDED result with polling evidence instead of treating 202 as completion
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback mock logs every request and the protected verifier checks the exact operation order, raw targets, fixed query, session header, and compact JSON wire body against the pinned VCF 9.1 vCenter OpenAPI contract
